title: prefill-decode-chunked-speculative-stage-overlap-kv-scheduler-kv-cache-optimizations
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Runtime: Prefill/decode pipeline optimizations - chunked prefill, speculative prefill heuristics, stage-overlap kernel scheduler improvements, and KV-cache hot-path reductions. Expect lower end-to-end latency for mixed workloads and improved throughput for long prefill contexts.
description: Motivation: mixed prefill+decode workloads were exposing inefficiencies in our pipeline: long prefill batches were blocking decode lanes, speculative prefill attempts wasted decode cycles on low-confidence prefixes, and kernel scheduling didn't optimally overlap prefill/ decode stages with KV cache hot-paths. This PR implements a combined set of optimizations: 1) chunked prefill: break very long prefill sequences into smaller chunks to improve scheduler granularity and reduce head-of-line blocking for decode; 2) speculative prefill heuristics: speculative prefill now runs only when model/route confidence and recent cache hit patterns exceed a tunable threshold to reduce wasted compute; 3) stage-overlap kernel scheduler: new scheduler allows overlapping prefill kernel execution with decode kernels where dependency-safe, improves kernel packing and reduces idle GPU time; 4) KV cache hot-path reductions: inline common hot-paths, reduce mutex contended regions during cache reads/writes, and add a fast-path for 1) single-shard hits and 2) prefix-cache hits. Approach: changes are additive and guarded behind a runtime feature-flag (perf_prefill_pipeline_v2) with safe fallbacks to the existing pipeline. We added telemetry for new counters (speculative_prefill_attempts, speculative_prefill_successes, chunked_prefill_slices) and canaryed the flag in perf-canary before rolling to dedicated clusters. Performance: benchmarked on the perf-canary cluster with GPT-like model profiles and mixed traffic (60% decode, 40% prefill) shows ~8-12% end-to-end latency reduction p50/p95, up to 22% throughput improvement for long-context prefill-heavy workloads, and ~15% reduction in peak GPU memory pressure due to chunking. Speculative prefill reduced wasted decode work by ~18% across the sampled traces. Compatibility: no API changes. Feature guarded, default enabled for canary and opt-in on Dedicated during rollout. Testing: unit tests for scheduler heuristics, integration tests on the decode pipeline, new stress test for concurrent KV-cache access, and perf benchmarks added to perf-canary. Rollout plan: canary -> staged rollout to Dedicated (small pool) -> full Dedicated/Hosted after 2 weeks of monitoring. Related work: follows earlier PRs addressing overlapping prefill/decode (see pr-49847, pr-48612, pr-46321) and ties into KV-cache refactors in ENG-1429. Linked Linear tickets: ENG-1429 (pipeline refactor), ENG-1590 (kernel scheduler).
